items.title: Home
items.text: striqt is a set of open-source python packages for batched real-time signal analysis on CPU or GPU, and rapid prototyping of bespoke radio environment sensors.

items.title: Basic CLI usage
items.text:
🏃 Run a batched acquisition and analysis for measurement or calibration, given a path to a YAML input specification:

sensor-sweep [OPTIONS] YAML_PATH

#  Selected options:
#  -d, --debug                if set, drop to IPython debug prompt on exception
#  -v, --verbose              verbosity (or -vv, or -vvv)

📈 Plot the data variables in captures contained in one sweep of a zarr archive, given a YAML plotting configuration specification:

plot-capture [OPTIONS] ZARR_PATH YAML_PATH

# Selected options:
#  -i, --interactive
#  --no-save          don't save the resulting plots

More detailed usage instructions for these tools can be discovered with the --help flag.

items.title: Python module APIs
items.text: The API is organized into python packages:

items.title: striqt.analysis
items.text:
Provides optimized and validated real-time signal analysis of complex-valued IQ baseband: * Power spectral density and spectrogram evaluation * Power detectors in various time-domain representation * Empirical statistical distributions * Cellular cyclic prefix and synchronization correlators * Extensible with custom measurements registered beside the built-in ones

Interoperability within the modern python data ecosystem: * Interchangeable across CPU (numpy) and GPU (cupy) in 32-bit floating point * Package as multi-dimensional xarray.Dataset objects - Detailed coordinates, units, and metadata across all axes * Load and save zarr dataset archive format for easy aggregation and dissemination local or cloud storage

items.title: striqt.sensor
items.text: Implements batch IQ data acquisition and resampling oriented toward test and measurement * Input power level calibration based on the Y-factor technique * Support for exact rational Fourier resampling on CPU/GPU * Multi-threaded acquisition, analysis, and archival to maximize throughput * Software-defined radio interoperability via SoapySDR * Acquisition and analysis input specification schema (and yaml input decode support)

items.title: striqt.figures
items.text: Implements visualization for the data variables produced by striqt.analysis * Provides a plot function for each type of data variable * Uses the labeled coordinates and metadata to display proper units * Generates plots with matplotlib or plotly through one backend protocol

items.title: Installation
items.text: The following assume access to the open internet.

items.title: Option 1: pixi environment
items.text:
The repository carries a pixi manifest with the conda-forge dependencies, including SoapySDR, and a cupy environment for CUDA GPUs:

  1. Install pixi and clone this repository
  2. In the repository, run pixi install -e py315 (CPU) or pixi install -e cupy (CUDA GPU, linux or windows)
  3. Run the tools through the environment, for example pixi run -e py315 sensor-sweep --help

items.title: Option 2: pip installation
items.text:
An environment for post-analysis, plotting, and testing can be installed from the repository:

pip install "striqt @ git+https://github.com/usnistgov/striqt"

A lockfile (through uv, pixi, or pipenv) pins the dependency versions of an install; a container or virtual environment isolates it from other packages.

NOTE: SoapySDR is required to acquire radio captures. It is distributed on conda-forge, not on pypi.

items.title: Development status
items.text: striqt is in early beta. * The API in the base of each package is expected not to change, but internals (.lib, etc.) may change without warning * The yaml schemas of striqt.sensor and striqt.figures, and the CLI options, may still change * The data variable, coordinate, and metadata field names in .zarr files follow the names in the yaml schemas

items.title: measurement
items.text:
measurement(
    spec_type: type[Analysis],
    *,
    dtype: str,
    standard_name: str,
    long_name: str,
    units: str | None = None,
    dims: tuple[str, ...] | str | None = None,
    coord_factories: Iterable[CoordFunc]
    | CoordFunc
    | None = None,
    depends: Iterable[Callable] | Callable = (),
    caches: Iterable[KwArgCache] | KwArgCache | None = None,
    store_compressed: bool = True,
    prefer_filtered: bool = True,
    prefer_aligned: bool = True,
    validate: AnalysisValidator | None = None,
    tolerance: AnalysisTolerance | None = None,
) -> AnalysisFuncWrapper[P]

register the decorated function as the measurement configured by spec_type.

The returned decorator adds an entry to this registry. The decorated function is called as func(x, capture, **spec.to_dict()) with x an array of shape (port, sample). The function returns an array with a leading port axis followed by dims, or an (array, attrs) tuple. The returned wrapper is called as wrapper(iq, capture, as_xarray=True, **kwargs) with the fields of spec_type as keywords. The __signature__ of the wrapper is filled from spec_type. The docstring placeholders are filled at registration: {args} from the fields of spec_type, {dtype} from dtype, {dims} with the dimension names of the output (port first), {coords} with one bullet per coord_factories entry, and {attrs} with one bullet per registered attr other than standard_name and long_name.

An array iq is passed to the function as x. From an AcquiredIQ, x is the waveform that AcquiredIQ.preprocess selects for prefer_filtered and prefer_aligned. validate runs before the IQ is read and raises specs.helpers.SpecValidationError on a rejected combination. A units in a power form (striqt.waveform.units.DB_POWER, POWER, or AMPLITUDE) is resolved into the power_units of the acquisition when the output is built. A literal unit such as the ratio 'dB' is stored as written. The fields of the spec and the attrs returned by the function are added to the registered attrs, and a key set in both takes the value from the function.

The wrapper returns, by as_xarray:

  • True: an xarray.DataArray with a leading port dimension
  • 'delayed': a DelayedDataArray
  • False: the (array, attrs) pair

Parameters:

  • spec_type (type[Analysis]) –

    the specs.Analysis subclass with the keyword arguments of the measurement as fields, registered once

  • dtype (str) –

    numpy dtype name of the output array

  • standard_name (str) –

    the short noun phrase that names the output on an axis, stored as the standard_name attr

  • long_name (str) –

    the sentence-case title of the measurement for a plot or a menu, stored as the long_name attr

  • units (str | None, default: None ) –

    the units of the output values, stored as the units attr, or None for a dimensionless output

  • dims (tuple[str, ...] | str | None, default: None ) –

    the dimension names of the output axes after port, or None for the dimensions that coord_factories declare, in order

  • coord_factories (Iterable[CoordFunc] | CoordFunc | None, default: None ) –

    functions registered with coordinates that produce the coordinate values along dims from (capture, spec)

  • depends (Iterable[Callable] | Callable, default: () ) –

    measurements with an intermediate that this measurement reuses, recorded on the AnalysisInfo entry and not otherwise read

  • caches (Iterable[KwArgCache] | KwArgCache | None, default: None ) –

    the KwArgCache instances that cache_context enables for one capture, shared with the other measurements that list the same cache

  • store_compressed (bool, default: True ) –

    False to store the output uncompressed in zarr

  • prefer_filtered (bool, default: True ) –

    False to measure the waveform before the analysis_bandwidth low-pass, where one is applied

  • prefer_aligned (bool, default: True ) –

    False to measure the waveform before the signal-trigger shift, where one is applied. A signal_trigger measurement must set False

  • validate (AnalysisValidator | None, default: None ) –

    a function of (capture, spec) that raises on a rejected combination without reading IQ, called with the specs.AnalysisCapture projection of the capture

  • tolerance (AnalysisTolerance | None, default: None ) –

    a function of (capture, spec, *, array_backend, input_error) that returns the specs.Tolerance of the output without reading IQ

Returns:

  • AnalysisFuncWrapper[P] –

    a decorator that registers the decorated function and returns the wrapper

Raises:

  • ValueError –

    when spec_type is already registered

  • TypeError –

    when a coord_factories entry is not callable; from the returned decorator, when the function name is already registered or when caches contains something other than KwArgCache instances

items.title: cellular_5g_pss_correlation
items.text:
cellular_5g_pss_correlation(iq: Array | AcquiredIQ, capture: Capture, *, subcarrier_spacing: float, sample_rate: float = 7680000.0, discovery_periodicity: float = 0.02, frequency_offset: float = 0, shared_spectrum: bool = False, delay: float = 0, symbol_indexes: one of ['auto', 'a', 'b', 'c', 'd', 'e', 'f', 'g'] | tuple[int, ...] = 'auto', max_lag_symbols: int | None = None, max_block_count: int | None = 1, as_xarray: bool | Literal['delayed'] = True) -> Measurement

correlate each port of the IQ against the 5G NR primary synchronization signal.

The input is the IQ before the analysis_bandwidth filter and before trigger alignment. The band at frequency_offset is shifted to baseband and resampled to sample_rate. The result is cross-correlated with the PSS sequence of each cell sector ID (3GPP TS 38.211 §7.4.2.2). The PSS template has unit energy over the 127 PSS subcarriers. The squared magnitude of a peak on a lag sample equals the received PSS symbol power. White noise with power spectral density N0 has a mean squared magnitude of N0 * subcarrier_spacing in each lag.

Output
  • Array dtype: complex64
  • Dimensions: port, cellular_cell_id2, cellular_ssb_start_time, cellular_ssb_beam_index, cellular_ssb_lag

  • Coordinates:

  • cellular_cell_id2 (uint16): sector part of the physical cell ID of each sync template, 0 through 2

  • cellular_ssb_start_time (float32, s): start time of each sync block in the capture, in steps of discovery_periodicity, up to max_block_count blocks
  • cellular_ssb_beam_index (uint16): index of each candidate sync block in the burst set, in the order of symbol_indexes
  • cellular_ssb_lag (float32, s): lag of each correlation sample from the start of the IQ, from delay in steps of one sample at sample_rate, spanning max_lag_symbols OFDM symbols or the SSB when None

  • Attributes:

  • units: power units based on acquisition (√mW when calibrated)

  • noise_bandwidth: subcarrier_spacing (in Hz)
References

3GPP TS 38.211, "NR; Physical channels and modulation," Table 7.4.3.1-1 and §7.4.2.2. https://www.3gpp.org/DynaReport/38211.htm

3GPP TS 38.213, "NR; Physical layer procedures for control," §4.1. https://www.3gpp.org/DynaReport/38213.htm

Parameters:

  • iq (Array or AcquiredIQ) –

    the IQ waveform with shape (port, sample), or an AcquiredIQ from which the conditioned waveform is selected

  • capture (Capture) –

    the acquisition parameters of iq

  • as_xarray (bool or delayed, default: True ) –

    True for an xarray.DataArray, False for an (array, attrs) tuple, or 'delayed' for a DelayedDataArray

  • subcarrier_spacing (float) –

    Subcarrier spacing (15e3, 30e3, 60e3, etc) (Constraints: units: Hz)

  • sample_rate (float, default: 7680000.0 ) –
  • discovery_periodicity (float, default: 0.02 ) –
  • frequency_offset (float, default: 0 ) –
  • shared_spectrum (bool, default: False ) –
  • delay (float, default: 0 ) –
  • symbol_indexes (one of ['auto', 'a', 'b', 'c', 'd', 'e', 'f', 'g'] | tuple[int, ...], default: 'auto' ) –

    index locations in the SSB, or a cell search case from 3GPP TS 38.213 Sec. 4.1)

  • max_lag_symbols (int | None, default: None ) –

    limit the number of symbols of lag in the 5G sync correlator (Constraints: >= 1, <= 6)

  • max_block_count (int | None, default: 1 ) –

items.title: cellular_5g_ssb_spectrogram
items.text:
cellular_5g_ssb_spectrogram(
    iq: Array | AcquiredIQ,
    capture: Capture,
    *,
    subcarrier_spacing: float,
    sample_rate: float = 7680000.0,
    discovery_periodicity: float = 0.02,
    frequency_offset: float = 0,
    max_block_count: int | None = None,
    window: str | tuple[str, float] = 'blackmanharris',
    lo_bandstop: float | None = None,
    as_xarray: bool | Literal['delayed'] = True,
) -> Measurement

evaluate a spectrogram of each 5G NR SSB burst set by OFDM symbol and subcarrier.

The input is the IQ before the analysis_bandwidth filter and after trigger alignment. The STFT hops once per OFDM symbol. Half-subcarrier bins are summed pairwise to one bin per subcarrier of subcarrier_spacing. Only the symbols of the burst set in the first 2 ms of each discovery_periodicity are kept (3GPP TS 38.213 §4.1).

Output
  • Array dtype: float16
  • Dimensions: port, cellular_ssb_index, cellular_ssb_symbol_index, cellular_ssb_baseband_frequency

  • Coordinates:

  • cellular_ssb_index (uint16): index of each burst set in the capture, one per discovery_periodicity, up to max_block_count burst sets

  • cellular_ssb_symbol_index (uint16): index of each OFDM symbol in the first 2 ms of the burst set, at subcarrier_spacing
  • cellular_ssb_baseband_frequency (float64, Hz): baseband frequency of each subcarrier relative to frequency_offset, in steps of subcarrier_spacing across the sample_rate band

  • Attributes:

  • units: power units based on acquisition (dBm when calibrated)

  • noise_bandwidth: subcarrier_spacing (in Hz)
  • resolution_bandwidth: equivalent noise bandwidth (in Hz) of the nonzero samples of window
  • limit_digits: 3, the decimal places of the rounding
References

3GPP TS 38.213, "NR; Physical layer procedures for control," §4.1. https://www.3gpp.org/DynaReport/38213.htm

Parameters:

  • iq (Array or AcquiredIQ) –

    the IQ waveform with shape (port, sample), or an AcquiredIQ from which the conditioned waveform is selected

  • capture (Capture) –

    the acquisition parameters of iq

  • as_xarray (bool or delayed, default: True ) –

    True for an xarray.DataArray, False for an (array, attrs) tuple, or 'delayed' for a DelayedDataArray

  • subcarrier_spacing (float) –

    Subcarrier spacing (15e3, 30e3, 60e3, etc) (Constraints: units: Hz)

  • sample_rate (float, default: 7680000.0 ) –
  • discovery_periodicity (float, default: 0.02 ) –
  • frequency_offset (float, default: 0 ) –
  • max_block_count (int | None, default: None ) –
  • window (str | tuple[str, float], default: 'blackmanharris' ) –

    window function specification following scipy.signal.get_window

  • lo_bandstop (float | None, default: None ) –

    mask with float("nan") at this bandwidth centered at baseband DC (Constraints: units: Hz)

items.title: cellular_5g_sss_correlation
items.text:
cellular_5g_sss_correlation(iq: Array | AcquiredIQ, capture: Capture, *, subcarrier_spacing: float, sample_rate: float = 7680000.0, discovery_periodicity: float = 0.02, frequency_offset: float = 0, shared_spectrum: bool = False, delay: float = 0, symbol_indexes: one of ['auto', 'a', 'b', 'c', 'd', 'e', 'f', 'g'] | tuple[int, ...] = 'auto', max_lag_symbols: int | None = None, max_block_count: int | None = 1, as_xarray: bool | Literal['delayed'] = True) -> Measurement

correlate each port of the IQ against the 5G NR secondary synchronization signal.

The input is the IQ before the analysis_bandwidth filter and before trigger alignment. The band at frequency_offset is shifted to baseband and resampled to sample_rate. The result is cross-correlated with the SSS sequences (3GPP TS 38.211 §7.4.2.3). The SSS template has unit energy over the 127 SSS subcarriers. The squared magnitude of a peak on a lag sample equals the received SSS symbol power. White noise with power spectral density N0 has a mean squared magnitude of N0 * subcarrier_spacing in each lag.

Output
  • Array dtype: complex64
  • Dimensions: port, cellular_cell_id2, cellular_ssb_start_time, cellular_ssb_beam_index, cellular_ssb_lag

  • Coordinates:

  • cellular_cell_id2 (uint16): sector part of the physical cell ID of each sync template, 0 through 2

  • cellular_ssb_start_time (float32, s): start time of each sync block in the capture, in steps of discovery_periodicity, up to max_block_count blocks
  • cellular_ssb_beam_index (uint16): index of each candidate sync block in the burst set, in the order of symbol_indexes
  • cellular_ssb_lag (float32, s): lag of each correlation sample from the start of the IQ, from delay in steps of one sample at sample_rate, spanning max_lag_symbols OFDM symbols or the SSB when None

  • Attributes:

  • units: power units based on acquisition (√mW when calibrated)

  • noise_bandwidth: subcarrier_spacing (in Hz)
References

3GPP TS 38.211, "NR; Physical channels and modulation," Table 7.4.3.1-1 and §7.4.2.3. https://www.3gpp.org/DynaReport/38211.htm

3GPP TS 38.213, "NR; Physical layer procedures for control," §4.1. https://www.3gpp.org/DynaReport/38213.htm

Parameters:

  • iq (Array or AcquiredIQ) –

    the IQ waveform with shape (port, sample), or an AcquiredIQ from which the conditioned waveform is selected

  • capture (Capture) –

    the acquisition parameters of iq

  • as_xarray (bool or delayed, default: True ) –

    True for an xarray.DataArray, False for an (array, attrs) tuple, or 'delayed' for a DelayedDataArray

  • subcarrier_spacing (float) –

    Subcarrier spacing (15e3, 30e3, 60e3, etc) (Constraints: units: Hz)

  • sample_rate (float, default: 7680000.0 ) –
  • discovery_periodicity (float, default: 0.02 ) –
  • frequency_offset (float, default: 0 ) –
  • shared_spectrum (bool, default: False ) –
  • delay (float, default: 0 ) –
  • symbol_indexes (one of ['auto', 'a', 'b', 'c', 'd', 'e', 'f', 'g'] | tuple[int, ...], default: 'auto' ) –

    index locations in the SSB, or a cell search case from 3GPP TS 38.213 Sec. 4.1)

  • max_lag_symbols (int | None, default: None ) –

    limit the number of symbols of lag in the 5G sync correlator (Constraints: >= 1, <= 6)

  • max_block_count (int | None, default: 1 ) –

items.title: cellular_cyclic_autocorrelation
items.text:
cellular_cyclic_autocorrelation(iq: Array | AcquiredIQ, capture: Capture, *, subcarrier_spacings: float | tuple[float, ...] = (15000.0, 30000.0, 60000.0), frame_range: int | tuple[int, int] = (0, 1), frame_slots: str | None = None, symbol_range: int | tuple[int, int | None] = (0, None), generation: one of ['4G', '5G'] = '5G', as_xarray: bool | Literal['delayed'] = True) -> Measurement

evaluate the cyclic-prefix autocorrelation of the IQ at each 4G or 5G symbol lag.

The input is the IQ after the analysis_bandwidth filter and before trigger alignment. For each spacing in subcarrier_spacings, the IQ is correlated with a copy of the IQ delayed by one OFDM symbol. The products are summed over the cyclic-prefix samples of the symbols selected by frame_range and symbol_range. The downlink slots and the uplink slots of frame_slots are summed separately. The output is the correlation magnitude. Entries past the symbol length of a spacing are nan. The 'uplink' row is nan when frame_slots has no uplink slot. frame_range and symbol_range are a count of indexes from 0, or a (start, stop) pair as for the Python builtin range.

Output
  • Array dtype: float32
  • Dimensions: port, link_direction, subcarrier_spacing, cyclic_sample_lag

  • Coordinates:

  • link_direction (str): TDD link direction of the summed slots, 'downlink' then 'uplink'

  • subcarrier_spacing (float32, Hz): subcarrier spacing of each numerology, in the order of subcarrier_spacings
  • cyclic_sample_lag (float32, s): lag of each autocorrelation sample, in steps of one sample at the capture sample_rate, spanning one OFDM symbol with cyclic prefix at the smallest of subcarrier_spacings

  • Attributes:

  • units: power units based on acquisition (mW when calibrated)

  • frames: the value of frame_range
  • symbols: the value of symbol_range

Parameters:

  • iq (Array or AcquiredIQ) –

    the IQ waveform with shape (port, sample), or an AcquiredIQ from which the conditioned waveform is selected

  • capture (Capture) –

    the acquisition parameters of iq

  • as_xarray (bool or delayed, default: True ) –

    True for an xarray.DataArray, False for an (array, attrs) tuple, or 'delayed' for a DelayedDataArray

  • subcarrier_spacings (float | tuple[float, ...], default: (15000.0, 30000.0, 60000.0) ) –

    One or more subcarrier spacings (15e3, 30e3, 60e3, etc) (Constraints: units: Hz)

  • frame_range (int | tuple[int, int], default: (0, 1) ) –
  • frame_slots (str | None, default: None ) –

    string composed of ('d', 'u', 's') specifying the sequence of slots in 1 TDD cellular frame, or None to fill with downlink

  • symbol_range (int | tuple[int, int | None], default: (0, None) ) –
  • generation (one of ['4G', '5G'], default: '5G' ) –

items.title: cellular_resource_power_histogram
items.text:
cellular_resource_power_histogram(iq: Array | AcquiredIQ, capture: Capture, *, window: str | tuple[str, float], subcarrier_spacing: float, power_low: float, power_high: float, power_resolution: float, average_rbs: bool | one of ['half'] = False, average_slots: bool = False, guard_bandwidths: tuple[float, float] = (0, 0), frame_slots: str | None = None, special_symbols: str | None = None, cyclic_prefix: one of ['normal', 'extended'] = 'normal', lo_bandstop: float | None = None, as_xarray: bool | Literal['delayed'] = True) -> Measurement

evaluate the fraction of resource grid elements in each power bin per link.

The input is the IQ before the analysis_bandwidth filter and after trigger alignment. The spectrogram has one bin per subcarrier, or per resource block with average_rbs, and one hop per OFDM symbol. frame_slots and special_symbols split the symbols into downlink and uplink. With average_slots, the power is averaged over each slot. The fractions of both link directions together sum to 1 on each port. Subcarriers inside the guard_bandwidths and flexible symbols are excluded from the count.

Output
  • Array dtype: float32
  • Dimensions: port, link_direction, cellular_resource_power_bin

  • Coordinates:

  • link_direction (str): TDD link direction of the summed slots, 'downlink' then 'uplink'

  • cellular_resource_power_bin (float32, dBm when calibrated): center of each power bin, from power_low to power_high in steps of power_resolution, with -inf and inf catch-all bins at each end

  • Attributes:

  • noise_bandwidth: subcarrier_spacing (in Hz), times 6 when average_rbs is 'half' and times 12 when True

  • resolution_bandwidth: equivalent noise bandwidth (in Hz) of the nonzero samples of window
  • limit_digits: None; the fractions are not rounded

Parameters:

  • iq (Array or AcquiredIQ) –

    the IQ waveform with shape (port, sample), or an AcquiredIQ from which the conditioned waveform is selected

  • capture (Capture) –

    the acquisition parameters of iq

  • as_xarray (bool or delayed, default: True ) –

    True for an xarray.DataArray, False for an (array, attrs) tuple, or 'delayed' for a DelayedDataArray

  • window (str | tuple[str, float]) –

    window function specification following scipy.signal.get_window

  • subcarrier_spacing (float) –

    Subcarrier spacing (15e3, 30e3, 60e3, etc) (Constraints: units: Hz)

  • power_low (float) –

    Minimum power bin (Constraints: units: dB power)

  • power_high (float) –

    Maximum power bin (Constraints: units: dB power)

  • power_resolution (float) –

    Power bin resolution (Constraints: units: dB)

  • average_rbs (bool | one of ['half'], default: False ) –

    frequency resolution of the spectrogram: False for 1 subcarrier, True for 1 resource block (12 subcarriers), or 'half' for 6 subcarriers

  • average_slots (bool, default: False ) –

    True to coarsen spectrogram bins by averaging 1-symbol time resolution

  • guard_bandwidths (tuple[float, float], default: (0, 0) ) –

    Bandwidths excluded at the (low, high) edges of the analysis band (Constraints: units: Hz)

  • frame_slots (str | None, default: None ) –

    string composed of ('d', 'u', 's') specifying the sequence of slots in 1 TDD cellular frame, or None to fill with downlink

  • special_symbols (str | None, default: None ) –

    string composed of the characters ('d', 'u', 'f') indicating the sequence of symbol types (when 's' is in frame_slots)

  • cyclic_prefix (one of ['normal', 'extended'], default: 'normal' ) –

    cyclic prefix length of the 3GPP numerology (TS 38.211 Table 4.2-1)

  • lo_bandstop (float | None, default: None ) –

    mask with float("nan") at this bandwidth centered at baseband DC (Constraints: units: Hz)

items.title: cyclic_channel_power
items.text:
cyclic_channel_power(
    iq: Array | AcquiredIQ,
    capture: Capture,
    *,
    cyclic_period: float,
    detector_period: Fraction,
    power_detectors: tuple[str, ...] = ('rms', 'peak'),
    cyclic_statistics: tuple[str | float, ...] = (
        'min',
        'mean',
        'max',
    ),
    as_xarray: bool | Literal['delayed'] = True,
) -> Measurement

evaluate cyclic statistics of channel power across the cycles in a capture.

The input is the IQ after the analysis_bandwidth filter and trigger alignment. Each power detector bins the capture on detector_period. The binned series is folded into cycles of cyclic_period. Each cyclic statistic reduces across the cycles (Kuester et al.). cyclic_period and detector_period alone set the trace length, independent of the capture duration.

A signal with a period that divides cyclic_period resolves at fixed lags with little spread between the 'min' and 'max' statistics. A cyclic_period of 10 ms covers TDD cellular frames, 5 ms covers WiMAX frames, and 1 ms covers the CBRS test bin 1 pulse repetition interval. The uplink and downlink levels of a TDD network then occupy disjoint lag windows. Occupancy with an incommensurate period smears across all lags.

Statistics are evaluated in linear power and converted to dB afterward. The capture duration must be a whole number of cycles. cyclic_period must be a whole number of detector periods. detector_period must be a whole number of samples at sample_rate. A detector_period written as a fraction stays exact, e.g., 1/28000 s for one OFDM symbol at 30 kHz subcarrier spacing. The noise bandwidth of the values is the analysis_bandwidth of the capture, or sample_rate where analysis_bandwidth is infinite.

Output
  • Array dtype: float32
  • Dimensions: port, power_detector, cyclic_statistic, cyclic_lag

  • Coordinates:

  • power_detector (object): power detector of each trace, in the order of power_detectors

  • cyclic_statistic (object): statistic of each trace, in the order of cyclic_statistics
  • cyclic_lag (float32, s): time from the start of each cycle, in steps of detector_period over one cyclic_period

  • Attributes:

  • units: power units based on acquisition (dBm when calibrated)

References

D. G. Kuester et al., "Cyclic Analysis of Power in Radio Channels."

Parameters:

  • iq (Array or AcquiredIQ) –

    the IQ waveform with shape (port, sample), or an AcquiredIQ from which the conditioned waveform is selected

  • capture (Capture) –

    the acquisition parameters of iq

  • as_xarray (bool or delayed, default: True ) –

    True for an xarray.DataArray, False for an (array, attrs) tuple, or 'delayed' for a DelayedDataArray

  • cyclic_period (float) –

    Cycle period of the channel power statistics, a whole multiple of detector_period and a common multiple of the expected signal periods (Constraints: units: s)

  • detector_period (Fraction) –

    Power detector bin duration, a whole multiple of the sample period (Constraints: units: s)

  • power_detectors (tuple[str, ...], default: ('rms', 'peak') ) –

    Power detectors evaluated in each bin: 'rms', 'peak', or both

  • cyclic_statistics (tuple[str | float, ...], default: ('min', 'mean', 'max') ) –

    Statistics evaluated across cycles at each cycle lag: 'min', 'mean', 'max', 'median', or a quantile in (0, 1)

items.text:
power_spectral_density(
    iq: Array | AcquiredIQ,
    capture: Capture,
    *,
    window: str | tuple[str, float],
    frequency_resolution: float,
    fractional_overlap: Fraction = 0,
    window_fill: Fraction = 1,
    integration_bandwidth: float | None = None,
    trim_stopband: bool = True,
    lo_bandstop: float | None = None,
    time_statistic: tuple[str | float, ...] = ('mean',),
    as_xarray: bool | Literal['delayed'] = True,
) -> Measurement

estimate the power spectral density from time statistics of the spectrogram.

The input is the IQ before the analysis_bandwidth filter and after trigger alignment. Each time_statistic reduces the unrounded linear-power spectrogram output over the STFT windows at each frequency bin. 'mean' is the Welch estimate (Welch, 1967). A float in [0, 1] is a quantile.

Output
  • Array dtype: float32
  • Dimensions: port, time_statistic, baseband_frequency

  • Coordinates:

  • time_statistic (str): name of each statistic, in the order of time_statistic

  • baseband_frequency (float64, Hz): baseband frequency of each bin, in steps of frequency_resolution about DC or of integration_bandwidth when set, truncated to a finite analysis_bandwidth when trim_stopband is set

  • Attributes:

  • units: power units based on acquisition (dBm when calibrated)

  • noise_bandwidth: the bandwidth (in Hz) that the values are referred to: frequency_resolution, or integration_bandwidth when set; the output minus 10 * log10(noise_bandwidth) is the density per Hz
  • resolution_bandwidth: the equivalent noise bandwidth (in Hz) of the nonzero samples of window
References

P. D. Welch, "The use of fast Fourier transform for the estimation of power spectra: A method based on time averaging over short, modified periodograms," IEEE Trans. Audio Electroacoust., vol. 15, no. 2, pp. 70-73, 1967. doi:10.1109/TAU.1967.1161901

    the IQ waveform with shape (port, sample), or an AcquiredIQ from which the conditioned waveform is selected

    the acquisition parameters of iq

  • as_xarray (bool or delayed, default: True ) –

    True for an xarray.DataArray, False for an (array, attrs) tuple, or 'delayed' for a DelayedDataArray

    window function specification following scipy.signal.get_window

  • lo_bandstop (float | None, default: None ) –

    mask with float("nan") at this bandwidth centered at baseband DC (Constraints: units: Hz)

  • time_statistic (tuple[str | float, ...], default: ('mean',) ) –

    power_high: float,

evaluate a histogram of the spectrogram power ratio between 2 ports.

The input is the IQ before the analysis_bandwidth filter and after trigger alignment. The spectrograms are the unrounded dB spectrograms of the same STFT fields as spectrogram. The ratio is the pixel-by-pixel difference of the 2 spectrograms in dB. The first output port is the ratio of the first input port to the second. The second output port is the negative of the first. items.title: circular_awgn
items.text:
circular_awgn(
    duration: float | None,
    sample_rate: float,
    *,
    power: float = 1.0,
    ports: int = 1,
    start_index: int = 0,
    count: int | None = None,
    seed: int = 0,
    xp: ModuleType = np,
    dtype: DTypeLike = 'complex64',
) -> Array

generate circularly-symmetric complex gaussian noise of total power power.

The real and imaginary parts are independent, each with variance power / 2. The mean of |iq|**2 is power. Each port is an independent draw. White noise with power spectral density noise_psd mW/Hz over the full sample rate has total power noise_psd * sample_rate mW.

Samples at indices i >= 0 are the stream from RandomState(seed), interleaved across ports within each sample. Samples at negative indices are drawn from a second stream seeded seed + 2**31, independent of the first stream and of the same power, with index -1 the first draw. A window at any start_index is the matching slice of any longer window.

Parameters:

  • duration (float | None) –

    capture duration, in s, used only when count is None

  • sample_rate (float) –

    IQ sample rate, in Hz, read only to convert duration to a sample count

  • power (float, default: 1.0 ) –

    total power of each port, in linear units

  • ports (int, default: 1 ) –

    number of receive ports, with independent noise on each port

  • start_index (int, default: 0 ) –

    absolute index of the first returned sample

  • count (int | None, default: None ) –

    number of samples, or None for duration less start_index

  • seed (int, default: 0 ) –

    seed of the noise generator, in [0, 2**31)

  • xp (ModuleType, default: np ) –

    the array namespace of the returned array

  • dtype (DTypeLike, default: 'complex64' ) –

    the returned complex dtype

Returns:

  • Array –

    an array of shape (ports, count) and dtype dtype in the namespace xp

Raises:

  • ValueError –

    when ports is below 1, when duration and count are both None, when the resolved count is negative, when seed is outside [0, 2**32), or when start_index is negative and seed is at or above 2**31

label an axis with the quantity and units named by the attrs of ax_data.

The label text is striqt.analysis.labels.quantity_label of the attrs. With a units attr, an EngFormatter with one SI prefix is set on each target axis. The prefix is striqt.waveform.units.si_prefix of the extent of the finite values, and is fixed for the axis. The prefixed units are in every tick label with tick_units True, or in the axis label with tick_units False, never in both. A label is set with or without finite values. items.title: open_resources
items.text:
open_resources(
    spec: ActionSpec[SS, SP, SA],
    spec_path: str | Path | None = None,
    *,
    test_only: bool = False,
    on_source_opened: SourceOpenCallback | None = None,
    on_analyzed: AnalyzedCallback | None = None,
    on_sink_cached: CachedCallback | None = None,
    select_analysis: AnalysisSelector | None = None,
) -> ConnectionManager[SS, SP, SC, SA, PS, PC]

open the sensor hardware and software contexts needed to run spec.

The source, peripherals, sink, calibration file, and log file open concurrently for the sweep of the action runner built from spec. The compute warmup runs in the calling thread. The returned ConnectionManager yields the open Resources on entry and closes every resource on exit. An exception from a hook ends the run. Progress is logged at INFO on the sweep logger.

Parameters:

  • spec (ActionSpec[SS, SP, SA]) –

    the action spec

  • spec_path (str | Path | None, default: None ) –

    the file from which spec was read, or None; the process working directory becomes the directory of the file, and the {spec_path} path field is set

  • test_only (bool, default: False ) –

    if True, open NoPeripherals in place of the peripherals and skip the compute warmup

  • on_source_opened (SourceOpenCallback | None, default: None ) –

    hook run once with (sweep, source_id) in a worker thread after the source opens and before the first capture

  • on_analyzed (AnalyzedCallback | None, default: None ) –

    hook run in the analysis thread with the DelayedDataset of each acquisition, before the sink receives the dataset; the extra_data of the dataset lacks the peripheral entries

  • on_sink_cached (CachedCallback | None, default: None ) –

    hook run in the analysis thread with (resources, cache, capture, result, **kwargs) each time a measurement fills a KwArgCache

  • select_analysis (AnalysisSelector | None, default: None ) –

    hook run in the analysis thread with (capture, analysis) before each analysis, returning the group to evaluate in place of the adjusted analysis; a sink that allocates a store from the full group rejects the narrowed result

Raises:

  • TypeError –

    if no action runner is registered for the type of spec

  • KeyError –

    if no sensor binding is registered for the type of spec

  • ExceptionGroup –

    if more than one resource fails to open; a single failure raises that exception

read the IQ of one burst segment of the armed capture.

The read of segment 0, or of a segment with resume, triggers the backend and applies the transient holdoff. The read of a later segment continues the enabled stream from the samples carried over after the previous segment. The carryover is kept for the next segment and cleared after the last segment of the burst.

  • burst_index (int, default: 0 ) –

  • resume (bool, default: False ) –

    if True, segment burst_index is read as the first segment after a stream error, with no carryover

  • tuple[Array, int | None] –

items.title: acquire_burst
items.text:
acquire_burst(
    overlaps: tuple[int, int] | None = None,
    *,
    queue: AcquisitionQueue | None = None,
    finalize: Callable[[AcquiredIQ], AcquiredIQ]
    | None = None,
) -> list[AcquiredIQ]

acquire the capture.burst segments of the armed capture.

The segments are read back to back with the stream enabled. After a stream error or overflow during segment k, the backend runs prepare_retrigger and the read is repeated, up to source_info.retries times per burst. Under bursts.on_gap='skip', segment k is read again as a first segment. Under 'except', the segments of the burst still in queue are removed and the burst restarts from segment 0.

Each segment passes through finalize before it is queued or returned. When queue is full, the put of a segment of a capture with burst above 1 is skipped with a WARNING on the source logger under 'skip' and raises under 'except'. The put of a capture with burst 1 waits for a free slot.

Parameters:

  • overlaps (tuple[int, int] | None, default: None ) –

    the (lead, tail) overlap in source samples, or None to derive the overlap from the capture and the analysis target

  • queue (AcquisitionQueue | None, default: None ) –

    the queue that receives each segment, or None to return the segments

  • finalize (Callable[[AcquiredIQ], AcquiredIQ] | None, default: None ) –

    a function applied to each segment before the queue put

Returns:

  • list[AcquiredIQ] –

    the segments in order when queue is None, otherwise an empty list

Raises:

  • ValueError –

    if burst is above 1 and capture.duration is not a whole number of trigger_strobe periods

  • AcquisitionOverrunError –

    if queue is full under bursts.on_gap='except'

  • ReceiveStreamError –

    on a stream error once the retries are exhausted

  • OverflowError –

    on a stream overflow once the retries are exhausted

  • ThreadInterruptRequest –

    in a worker thread, when cancel_threads has been called

bind_sensor(
    key: str,
    sensor: Sensor[TS2, TP2, TC2],

    register: bool = True,
    *,
    module: Optional[str] = None,
) -> type[Controller[SS, SP, SC, SA, PS, PC]]

bind the implementation classes of a sensor to spec types under key.

The returned Controller subclass has the class attributes sensor (a SensorBinding) and schema. Its sensor.sweep_spec_cls is a subclass of the action spec type, tagged with key in the sensor_binding field. In that subclass, source, peripherals, captures (when the action declares the field), and analysis (when the action is a Sweep) are annotated with the types in schema. A sweep file with sensor_binding equal to key decodes to an instance of that subclass. The tagged subclass has the class attributes sensor, schema, controller (the returned class), and sweep_cls (the bound Sweep class with the same spec types, or the tagged subclass when the action is a Sweep). The tagged subclass of an unregistered binding is decoded only by explicit type.

Parameters:

    the sensor_binding value of sweep files, and the registry key

  • sensor (Sensor[TS2, TP2, TC2]) –

  • schema (Schema[SS, SP, SC, SA, PS, PC]) –

    the spec types; schema.action selects the action spec type and schema.analysis the analysis group

  • register (bool, default: True ) –

write the dataset of each acquisition into a zarr store allocated for the whole sweep.

open allocates every data variable and coordinate of the store from the sweep spec, with one row per port per burst segment of every expanded capture along capture, and keeps the metadata in memory until each append for a directory store or until close for a zip store. The power units attrs of the allocated variables and coordinates are in the power family of the source. append places the arrays of a DelayedDataset on the union grid of the sweep and writes every chunk that the acquisition completes. Each chunk is written once. A burst segment re-acquired after a stream overflow is a further row: (capture_index, burst_index) may repeat, with a later start_time. close writes the partial chunks, trims the store to the rows written, and consolidates the metadata.

A capture with the center_frequency of the channel is acquired at the sample rate that striqt.waveform.comms_5gnr.nr_sample_rate derives from channel_bandwidth and subcarrier_spacing, at or above min_sample_rate, with analysis_bandwidth equal to channel_bandwidth. The cellular measurement parameters are set from the remaining fields through the adjust_analysis of the capture, with ssb_case None selecting the TS 38.213 §4.1 case for the spacing ('c' at 30 kHz). Only a subcarrier_spacing of 30 kHz is accepted, and tdd_frame_slots is 1 character per slot of the 10 ms frame or 1 character for every slot.

Each field is named for a measurement, and None disables the measurement. A block enables the measurement and holds only the parameters that the channel does not fix. The remaining parameters are set from the cell_channels entry at the center frequency of the capture and from the subcarrier spacing, or stay at the measurement default.

items.title: Cellular5GNRSweep
items.text:
Bases: CapturePlan[SS, SP, SC, SA]

the spec of a sweep over 5G NR channels.

Each entry of captures names a channel by center_frequency, and cell_channels maps a label to the CellChannel at that frequency. The sample_rate and analysis_bandwidth of a capture are left at the class defaults and set from the matched channel. A loop over center_frequency is rejected, two cell_channels entries must not share a center_frequency, and every channel in use must share one subcarrier spacing.

items.title: design_cola_resampler
items.text:
design_cola_resampler(
    fs_base: float,
    fs_target: float,
    bw: float = inf,
    bw_lo: float = 0,
    min_oversampling: float = 1.1,
    min_fft_size=2 * 4096 - 1,
    shift: ShiftType = False,
    window=None,
    fs_sdr: Optional[float] = None,
) -> ResamplerDesign

design the radio sample rate, LO offset, and COLA FFT sizes of a resampler.

nfft / nfft_out equals fs_sdr / fs_target exactly. The sizes are k * p and k * q for the reduced ratio p / q of fs_sdr to fs_target, with k the smallest even multiple of the COLA divisor of window that is 2·3·5·7-smooth and puts nfft_out above min_fft_size. Without fs_sdr, the radio rate is fs_base divided by the largest integer that keeps the rate at or above fs_target + min_oversampling * bw + bw_lo with shift, or at or above fs_target without. With shift, the radio is tuned lo_offset below the center frequency, and the magnitude of lo_offset is bw / 2 + bw_lo / 2 rounded up to a whole number of fs_sdr / nfft bins that is a multiple of the frames per hop of window.

Parameters:

  • fs_base (float) –

    the master clock rate (in S/s) that fs_sdr divides

  • fs_target (float) –

    the sample rate (in S/s) after resampling

  • bw (float, default: inf ) –

    the bandwidth (in Hz) to protect from LO leakage; inf disables the LO shift and leaves the passband unbounded

  • bw_lo (float, default: 0 ) –

    the bandwidth (in Hz) of the LO leakage and phase noise kept out of the protected band

  • min_oversampling (float, default: 1.1 ) –

    the factor applied to bw when sizing fs_sdr for an LO shift

  • min_fft_size –

    the size that nfft_out must exceed

  • shift (ShiftType, default: False ) –

    'left' or 'right' places the protected band below or above the tuned LO; 'none', None, or False leaves the LO at the center frequency

  • window –

    a key of the COLA window divisor table; None selects the divisor 1 for the sizes and the LO offset, and 'hann' in the result

  • fs_sdr (Optional[float], default: None ) –

    the radio sample rate (in S/s) to use instead of selecting one

Returns:

  • ResamplerDesign –

    the ResamplerDesign that resamples from the selected radio rate to

  • ResamplerDesign –

    fs_target

Raises:

  • ValueError –

    if shift is set while bw is infinite, shift is not a recognized direction, window has no COLA divisor, bw exceeds fs_base, the LO shift needs a radio rate above fs_base, no fraction with denominator up to OLA_MAX_FFT_SIZE realizes the rate ratio, or the LO shift does not fit the Nyquist band of the radio at fs_sdr

items.title: equivalent_noise_bandwidth
items.text:
equivalent_noise_bandwidth(
    window: WindowSpecType, N, fftbins=True, cached=True
)

return the equivalent noise bandwidth (ENBW) of a window, in bins.

One bin is fs / N wide for a window of N nonzero samples (Harris 1978). The ENBW in Hz is the returned value times fs / N. An FFT of the window zero-padded to N + nzero samples has bins of fs / (N + nzero). The same ENBW spans (N + nzero) / N times as many of those bins.

Parameters:

  • window (WindowSpecType) –

    the window name or (name, parameter) for get_window

  • N –

    the number of nonzero window samples

  • fftbins –

    the get_window periodic-window flag

  • cached –

    True designs the window through the cached get_window; False designs it uncached

Returns:

  • –

    the ENBW as a float: 1.0 for a rectangular window and larger for every other

References

F. J. Harris, "On the use of windows for harmonic analysis with the discrete Fourier transform," Proc. IEEE, vol. 66, no. 1, pp. 51-83, Jan. 1978.

oaresample(
    x: Array,
    up,
    down,
    fs,
    *,
    window: str | tuple[str, float] = 'hann',
    overwrite_x: bool = False,
    axis: int = 1,
    frequency_shift: float = 0,
    filter_bandwidth: float | None = None,
    transition_bandwidth: float = 250000.0,
    scale: Array | float = 1.0,
    out: Array | None = None,
)

resample x by up / down through STFT overlap-add.

Each STFT block of down samples is cropped or zero-padded to up bins, scaled by the low-pass response and scale, and overlap-added at the output rate. The response has the band edges of design_fir_lpf: the gain is 1/2 at filter_bandwidth / 2 and the transition is centered there.

Parameters:

  • x (Array) –

    the waveform, with time on axis; its length must be a whole number of STFT hops, down + k * (down - noverlap)

  • up –

    the output block size (in samples), an even multiple of the COLA divisor of window

  • down –

    the input block size (in samples), an even multiple of the COLA divisor of window

  • fs –

    the sample rate (in S/s) of x

  • window (str | tuple[str, float], default: 'hann' ) –

    the COLA window of the STFT, a key of the divisor table

  • overwrite_x (bool, default: False ) –

    True permits the STFT to consume the buffer of x; the contents of x are undefined after the call

  • axis (int, default: 1 ) –

    the time axis of x

  • frequency_shift (float, default: 0 ) –

    the frequency (in Hz) moved to the output DC, a multiple of fs / down times the frames per hop of window; 0 keeps the center frequency

  • filter_bandwidth (float | None, default: None ) –

    the passband width (in Hz) of the low-pass; None or inf applies no low-pass

  • transition_bandwidth (float, default: 250000.0 ) –

    the width (in Hz) of the low-pass transition band

  • scale (Array | float, default: 1.0 ) –

    a voltage gain, a scalar or one value per entry of the axis before axis

  • out (Array | None, default: None ) –

    a C-contiguous buffer of at least x.size * up // down elements in the dtype of x that receives the output; x itself is accepted when overwrite_x is True

Returns:

  • –

    the waveform at fs * up / down on axis, of ``x.shape[axis] * up //

  • –

    down` samples, in the dtype and array namespace ofx; a view ofout`

  • –

    when out is given

Raises:

  • ValueError –

    if frequency_shift is nonzero while upsampling, is not a multiple of fs / down times the frames per hop, or moves the output band past an edge of the input band; if up or down is odd or not a multiple of the COLA divisor; if window has no COLA divisor; if filter_bandwidth is finite and at most transition_bandwidth; or if out is not C-contiguous, has another dtype, has fewer than x.size * up // down elements, or shares memory with x without overwrite_x

items.title: iq_to_cyclic_power
items.text:
iq_to_cyclic_power(
    x: Array,
    Ts: float,
    detector_period: float,
    cyclic_period: float,
    truncate=False,
    detectors=('rms', 'peak'),
    cycle_stats=('min', 'mean', 'max'),
    axis=0,
) -> dict[str, dict[str, Array]]

return cyclic statistics of the channel power of x binned along axis.

Each detector in detectors bins the power of x along axis into K samples of detector_period. The detector series is indexed as a matrix of cycles and lags: sample k is in cycle k // L at lag (k % L) * detector_period, where L = cyclic_period / detector_period is the number of detector bins per cycle and M = K / L is the number of cycles. Each cyclic statistic reduces the cycle axis, so the value at lag m summarizes the M samples at the same offset from the start of a cycle. The result spans one cyclic_period at the resolution of detector_period, with L samples per detector and statistic, for any capture length.

With a cyclic_period that is a common multiple of the periods of the expected signals (e.g., 10 ms for TDD cellular frames, 5 ms WiMAX frames, and the 1 ms pulse repetition interval of the SPN-43 radar), the features of those signals fall at the same lags in every cycle. Occupancy with an incommensurate period is spread across all lags. The uplink and downlink levels of a TDD network fall in disjoint lag windows.

With a mismatch dT between cyclic_period and the signal period, such as from a sample clock offset, a feature drifts by M * dT / detector_period lags over the capture and bleeds into neighboring lags. The drift stays within one lag while M * dT is below detector_period, which bounds the usable number of cycles M.

Parameters:

  • x (Array) –

    the IQ waveform, complex or real, with time on axis

  • Ts (float) –

    sample period of the waveform (in s)

  • detector_period (float) –

    duration of each power detector bin (in s), an integer multiple of Ts

  • cyclic_period (float) –

    duration of one cycle (in s), an integer multiple of detector_period

  • truncate –

    True to drop trailing samples that do not complete a detector bin or a cycle, and to round detector_period to the nearest multiple of Ts

  • detectors –

    power detector names accepted by iq_to_bin_power

  • cycle_stats –

    statistics accepted by stat_ufunc_from_shorthand, evaluated across cycles (names such as 'min', 'mean', 'max', or quantiles in (0, 1))

  • axis –

    the time axis of x

Returns:

  • dict[str, dict[str, Array]] –

    dict keyed on detector, of dicts keyed on cyclic statistic, of arrays in the

  • dict[str, dict[str, Array]] –

    namespace of x with the axis dimension replaced by the L cycle lags,

  • dict[str, dict[str, Array]] –

    in linear power units; each statistic is evaluated on the linear power

Raises:

  • ValueError –

    if detectors is None; if cyclic_period is not an integer multiple of detector_period; or, when truncate is False, if detector_period is not an integer multiple of Ts or the capture does not contain a whole number of cycles

References

D.G. Kuester et al., "Cyclic Analysis of Power in Radio Channels".

si_prefix(
    values: Union[float, Iterable[float]],
    units: Union[str, None] = None,
    *,
    places: Union[int, None] = None,
) -> SIPrefix

return one SI prefix for every value of values in units.

The prefix is that of the largest finite nonzero magnitude, with a mantissa that rounds to 1000 under places carried to the next prefix. With two or more distinct magnitudes, the prefix is lowered to that of the step between the closest pair, by at most one prefix. Thus 3.7 and 3.75 GHz read as 3700 and 3750 MHz, and every mantissa stays below 10⁶. Units that are not is_prefixable, and values with no finite nonzero magnitude, give the exponent 0.

Parameters:

  • values (Union[float, Iterable[float]]) –

    one value, or the values to share the prefix; zero, NaN, and infinite values are ignored

  • units (Union[str, None], default: None ) –

    the units string of the values, or None for a bare number

  • places (Union[int, None], default: None ) –

    the decimal places the mantissas are shown with, or None for the shortest representation

items.text:
to_wave(units: str) -> str

return the amplitude (square root of power) form of a units string.

'dBm' and 'mW' give '√mW', and 'dB' gives '√unitless'. A string without a known base is returned unchanged.

items.title: with_power_units
items.text:
with_power_units(
    units: str, power_units: PowerUnits
) -> str

return units with its power unit replaced by power_units in the same form.

The dB, linear, or amplitude form and the denominator are kept: 'dBm/Hz' with 'FS' gives 'dBFS/Hz', and '√mW' with 'a.u.' gives '√a.u.'. A string that power_family does not recognize is returned unchanged.

items.title: Acquisition
items.text: The commands below run a sweep from a specification file and prepare the GPU kernels for one.

items.title: sensor-sweep
items.text:
run the sweep specified at PATH.

PATH is a YAML or JSON sweep specification. The results are written to the sink path in the specification, or to --output-path. A y/n prompt on the capture adjustments precedes a sweep that has any, unless --skip-confirm is given.

Usage:

sensor-sweep [OPTIONS] PATH

Options:

Name Type Description Default --debug, -d boolean invoke an IPython debug prompt on exception False --skip-confirm, -s boolean skip y/n confirmation before start False --verbose, -v integer range (0 and above) add detail to messages False --output-path, -o path override the output file path in the yaml specification None --help boolean Show this message and exit. Sentinel.UNSET

items.title: Datasets
items.text: The commands below plot, rechunk, archive, and serve the zarr datasets written by a sweep.

items.title: plot-capture
items.text:
plot the analysis results in the dataset at ZARR_PATH.

ZARR_PATH is a .zarr directory or .zarr.zip archive written by a sweep. YAML_PATH is a plot options file; when omitted, the plot options come from the plot_hint attribute of the dataset.

Usage:

plot-capture [OPTIONS] ZARR_PATH [YAML_PATH]

Options:

Name Type Description Default --interactive, -i choice (sixel | kitty) render the plots in the terminal through this graphics protocol None --no-save, -n boolean don't save the resulting plots False --help boolean Show this message and exit. Sentinel.UNSET

items.title: rechunk-zarr
items.text:
rechunk and recompress the zarr store at ZARR_INPUT into ZARR_OUTPUT.

ZARR_INPUT is a .zarr directory or .zarr.zip archive. ZARR_OUTPUT is the output store; when omitted, the output is written beside ZARR_INPUT with a timestamp suffix from the first start_time in the data. Each chunk holds --chunk-size MB, and a --compression level above 1 selects blosc zstd at that level.

Usage:

rechunk-zarr [OPTIONS] ZARR_INPUT [ZARR_OUTPUT]

Options:

Name Type Description Default --chunk-size integer size of each chunk (MB) 100 --compression integer compression level (0-9) 1 --help boolean Show this message and exit. Sentinel.UNSET

items.title: zip-zarr
items.text:
archive the zarr directory at ZARR_INPUT into a .zarr.zip file.

ZARR_INPUT is a .zarr store directory. ZARR_OUTPUT is the archive path; when omitted, the archive is written beside ZARR_INPUT with the .zip extension and a timestamp suffix from the first start_time in the data.

Usage:

zip-zarr [OPTIONS] ZARR_INPUT [ZARR_OUTPUT]

Options:

Name Type Description Default --remove / -r boolean delete ZARR_INPUT after the archive is written False --force / -f boolean overwrite an existing archive at the output path False --help boolean Show this message and exit. Sentinel.UNSET

items.title: web-plotter
items.text:
run a web-based real-time display for radio diagnostics.

PATH is the path to a JSON or YAML acquisition specification file.

Usage:

web-plotter [OPTIONS] PATH

Options:

Name Type Description Default --host, -h text Host to bind the server to 0.0.0.0 --port, -p integer Port to bind the server to 8000 --help boolean Show this message and exit. Sentinel.UNSET

items.title: Specs
items.text: The commands below inspect and convert sweep specification files.

items.title: check-sweep
items.text:
report the resources, paths, tolerances, and memory of the sweep at YAML_PATH.

YAML_PATH is a YAML sweep specification. The command opens the source, acquires no capture, and writes no store.

Usage:

check-sweep [OPTIONS] YAML_PATH

Options:

Name Type Description Default --help boolean Show this message and exit. Sentinel.UNSET

items.title: convert-spec
items.text:
convert the sweep specification at PATH between YAML and JSON.

PATH is a YAML (.yaml, .yml) or JSON (.json) sweep specification. The output is written beside PATH with the suffix .json, or .yaml with --yaml; a YAML input written as YAML takes the stem suffix -flat.

Usage:

convert-spec [OPTIONS] PATH

Options:

Name Type Description Default --yaml, -y boolean output a flattened yaml file instead of json False --help boolean Show this message and exit. Sentinel.UNSET
